title: Fix UI Border and Spacing Inconsistencies Across Panels
description: Refactor shared UI chrome to eliminate double borders and inconsistent spacing across the React shell (panels, tabs, trees, form controls) used by all sketchpad apps and playground/studio mode. Root causes: ButtonGroup/ButtonGroupItem double-draws borders on single-button usages (e.g. numberStepper +/- controls); ui-interpreter.tsx's renderUiControl mixes token spacing classes with raw untokenized Tailwind gap/padding across sibling control types; interpretUiNode's "stack" node uses a second, disconnected hardcoded-rem spacing scale via inline styles instead of the existing --ui-spacing token scale; several ad hoc bordered containers/dividers in ui-interpreter.tsx and os-shell.tsx use raw border-border instead of the existing borderNormalClass/borderElementClass/borderNormalBottomClass token classes; and nothing prevents adjacent containers from each independently drawing their own border-b divider (double dividers). Fix: correct the ButtonGroup primitive so a border is drawn exactly once; introduce a shared divide-based row-divider mechanism so dividers can't double by construction; tokenize all spacing/border usages in ui-interpreter.tsx and os-shell.tsx to use the existing ui/styling token scale; extend the existing regression test in ui/js/react/index.tsx (around line 25621) to guard against raw border-border and untokenized spacing regressions in these files going forward. Related to existing open ticket .repo/🎫/26/07/12/FIX-FORMS-BLUEPRINT-PANEL-LAYOUT-OVERLAP which touches the same stack-layout code in ui-interpreter.tsx.
summary: Fixed the visible double-border/inconsistent-spacing bugs in the forms Try panel and shell chrome. Root cause differed from the initial hypothesis: ButtonGroupItem never actually receives its `variant` prop (dead code), so the real bug was numberStepper hand-rolling three separately-bordered elements (Button, Input, Button) instead of reusing the existing single-bordered `Stepper` primitive. Fixes: (1) extended Stepper with `onDelta` (relative-delta path for click/drag/arrow-key increments, falls back to onChange) and `mixed` (blank/placeholder display for non-uniform multi-selection, mirroring Input's mixed prop) so it can fully replace the hand-rolled control; (2) rewired ui-interpreter.tsx's numberStepper case to render <Stepper> directly — eliminates the double/triple-border artifact visible in the screenshot; (3) tokenized renderUiControl's vec3/keyValue/slider spacing to the existing gap-single/gap-x-single/gap-y-single scale instead of raw untokenized gap-1/gap-2; (4) replaced interpretUiNode's stack-node inline style={{gap,padding}} (a second, disconnected hardcoded-rem spacing scale) with className-based tokens (gap-single/double/small, p-0/p-double) mapped proportionally from the old rem values, and replaced its ad hoc "border-border ... border" and the separator's raw <hr border-border> with borderElementClass/borderNormalTopClass; (5) swept os-shell.tsx's studio home/back chrome bars and color-swatch inputs off raw border-border/px-3 py-2/p-4 onto borderNormalBottomClass/borderElementClass/token padding; (6) extended the existing regression tests (ui/js/react/index.tsx's "uses normal shell edges..." test, and framework/renderer/react/index.test.ts's "declarative forms parity" describe block) with new assertions guarding the Stepper single-border invariant, the numberStepper mixed-state placeholder, and the stack node's tokenized gap/no-inline-style/no-border-border. Verified live in the forms dev preview (Geometry step, Offset X/Y/Z steppers): confirmed a single border renders per stepper group, zero border-border anywhere in the DOM, and the onDelta wiring works end-to-end (clicking + incremented the Y offset value). Did not touch ButtonGroup/ButtonGroupItem itself — investigation showed its border is drawn exactly once already (the outline variant's border is dead code, never forwarded), so no primitive fix was needed there. Did not find an actual double-divider bug in SidePanelChrome/PanelTabBar (they draw borders on different edges for different rows, which is correct), so no new divider-mechanism abstraction was introduced beyond the token fixes above.
